truth.problem: A Side-1 worker from the outgoing session can paint its result in the destination after a successful switch.
truth.impact: The destination transcript and worker status can contain stale data from an earlier session, violating AC2.

truth.problem: A foreground turn can start during asynchronous outgoing Slate preservation. Interactive resume now clears the busy flag even though the displaced foreground operation still owns its active token.
truth.impact: Before the old token settles, a destination prompt can bypass busy dispatch and throw from foregroundOperation.begin. The prompt that started in the preservation window is also canceled by the successful adoption.

truth.problem: Dismissing a busy recipient picker overwrites text typed while the decision journal opens the picker.
truth.impact: A second piece of unsent text disappears on Escape although no recipient was selected.

candidate.problem: The deny-by-default for shell approval is implemented by moving `recommended: true` onto the Deny option. In composer-choice.ts `recommended` drives the visible label (`choiceDisplayLabel` prefixes "(Recommended) ", line 26/508) and preselection is a separate field (`preselected`, lines 14-21, 34-39). So the change does more than change what a bare Enter does: every shell approval prompt now reads "(Recommended) Deny", for every command including harmless ones.
candidate.impact: An operator asked to approve an ordinary command (e.g. `ls`, `git status`) is told by the dialog that refusing it is the recommended answer. The safe-default goal only needs `preselected: true` on Deny; the label is an unintended side effect that misstates guidance on every prompt.

candidate.problem: The agent-shell Esc test builds its own wiring (`chrome.onEscapeInterrupt(() => foreground.cancel(...))` on a locally created ForegroundOperationOwner) instead of exercising the wiring this change adds in launchTuiAgentShell (tui-shell.ts:11946-11950). It proves that chrome.onEscapeInterrupt plus ForegroundOperationOwner.cancel abort a provider, not that the agent shell binds Esc. No source audit covers the production call either.
candidate.impact: Deleting or breaking the production binding at tui-shell.ts:11946 (the thing the footer hint "Esc interrupt" depends on in agent mode), or dropping its `◇ main turn interrupted (Esc)` notice, leaves this test and the rest of the suite green.
